"팀 브레인에 남기기" on one completed assistant turn creates a team-brain proposal citing that turn id; nothing is filed until the learner confirms.
Memory is scoped to one activity; a class or team activity never reads or writes the learner's personal memory, and the scope is fixed at activity creation.
Every action that sends learner content outside the activity (help request, collect, gallery, site publish, share) first lists what is sent, to whom, and what is excluded.

A learner may give a task an emoji and colour; the title remains the accessible name.
A personal task can move between personal activities; class tasks cannot leave their class activity.
Opening a non-class folder in a personal activity asks once whether Studio may read, edit and run files there; "제한 모드로 열기" keeps tools read-only.
"내 작품" lists the learner's artifacts across tasks of the current activity, newest change first.
Each artifact carries a provenance label derived from recorded events: AI가 만듦, 내가 올림, 내가 고침 (AI 결과를 사람이 수정).
Deleting a learner file through Studio moves it to the activity trash; it can be restored to its original path until the activity is removed.
"내 파일 붙이기" attaches existing files from the current workspace to the next message under existing attachment grants and caps.
From an artifact, "이 파일에 대해 묻기" opens the composer with that file attached and an editable starter line.
An artifact's info view links to the task and turn that created it and the turn that last changed it.
Each learner artifact has a visible version list (who changed it, when) and restore archives the current copy before replacing it.
Any send-to-others action states whether the receiver's AI may store the content.
When free disk space in the workspace volume falls below the threshold needed to save work, Studio warns before a turn writes files.
Each attachment failure cause has its own learner message and next step; the attachment chip and draft remain.
Downloads started in the Studio browser are saved into the activity's `downloads/` folder and report completion or failure in the chat timeline.
Memory is available only when the activity's Service profile enables it; minor cohorts default to off; the current state is visible in the activity.
The learner can view and delete each remembered item; a deleted item is absent from all later requests.
Memory capacity is shown as used/limit with a cleanup entry and no purchase control.
A memory overview lists stated facts grouped by task; it never contains ability, personality or capability statements.
An answer that used memory shows "기억 사용 N" listing the exact items; the learner can exclude an item from the rest of this task.
Every memory write appears as a timeline line in the turn that caused it, with an undo.
Each task has two switches, "이 작업에서 기억 쓰기" and "이 작업을 기억에 남기기"; "쓰기" locks after the first send.
In personal adult activities, "기록 없이 묻기" creates a task that is not persisted, not remembered and not spooled; it is unavailable in class activities with a reason.
Memory is stored as readable files inside the activity (`.hypeproof/memory/` or the team-brain folder) and the learner can open, read and delete them in Studio.
First enablement of memory shows once what is stored, where, who can read it and how to delete it; for minors the enablement happens in Chalk, not in a learner pop-up.
The learner can set a nickname the AI uses; no occupation or free "about me" field is collected for minor cohorts.
Help, collect, gallery and publish payloads exclude memory files unless the learner explicitly selects one.
Before gallery or site publish, Studio shows a visitor preview of exactly the published files and the audience.
At class end or trial→class transition, "내 작업 가져가기" lists what moves (files, tasks, team brain) and what does not (class materials, instructor notes, class memory), then reports per-item results.
When an activity can no longer run AI (class ended, token expired, cohort paused, budget exhausted), one status screen states the cause, what still works and who can fix it.
Chalk lessons can carry up to 4 conversation starters shown to learners as editable suggestions, and authoring shows that learners may elicit lesson material.
Chalk lets the instructor choose one approval preset per lesson version from `항상 묻기`, `중요한 것만 묻기`, `바꾸기 전에 묻기`; there is no full-access preset.
Studio shows the active approval preset next to the composer as read-only text.
Studio shows a "이 수업에서 AI가 할 수 있는 일" card derived from the resolved feature set (`read·write·shell·subagents·browser·web_search`) and the approval preset.

A command approval offers "이번 작업 동안 같은 종류 명령 허용" for a non-destructive command prefix. DEVIATION (2026-10-20, REQ-E1): ships as "이번 작업 동안 이 명령 허용" for the EXACT command only (whitespace collapsed); three adversarial verifications showed a prefix/"same kind" scope widens to code execution.
A write approval lists every file the tool call will change, in workspace-relative form.
A browser-open approval shows the destination host and whether it is the learner's own preview or the public internet.
Every denied tool call or disabled feature names its source: lesson setting, platform safety rule, or unsupported app version.
A model refusal on either runtime shows a composer banner with what the learner can still do.
When subagents are granted, the chat shows each delegation with helper name, delegated task, status and final response, plus "모두 멈추기".
The learner's goal is shown above the composer with status (진행 중 / 이룸 / 멈춤 / 예산 한도) and the remaining lesson budget.
A "계획 먼저 보기" toggle makes the coach return a numbered plan and perform no write/shell/browser tool until the learner approves the plan.
Chalk can schedule a lesson operation (open participation, pause new runs, release a prepared notice/prompt) at a KST date-time, once or weekly.
Each Chalk attention item has a title "state + object" and a summary "next step".
Chalk authoring assistant proposes lesson-setting changes as a card that changes nothing until the instructor presses Apply.
Chalk has one "수업 AI 설정" screen composing AI name/role/tone, instructions, model, effort, allowed features, approval preset and up to 4 starter prompts.
Before confirming a new lesson version, Chalk shows a per-field change list and an instruction text diff against the current version.
Chalk shows per-lesson AI usage: runs, active students, daily runs for 7 KST days.
The learner can open "AI가 기억하는 것" for the current project and download it.
Approval preset names and descriptions are shared between Chalk and Studio from one Service-owned catalog.
Studio shows the lesson's skills as a read-only shelf; the learner can view a skill's SKILL.md source and start "써 보기".
Chalk board uses five student states: 작업 중 / 막힘 / 선생님 확인 필요 / 쉬는 중 / 끝남, plus 확인 불가.
Studio's task list shows each task's AE-03 state, and one command moves focus to the next task waiting on the learner.
Studio notifies when the coach finishes a turn or waits for approval while the chat panel is not visible.
Chalk notifies the instructor when a student sends a help request.
Each task has a "바뀐 것" panel listing changed files with before/after and restore.
Adult website tracks can save a checkpoint with an AI-suggested message that the learner reviews.
When the task folder is missing, Studio shows a recovery notice with one action.
Shell rows show a purpose line, then `$ command` and the folder; a "실행 중인 것" list shows background processes with stop.
Adult/instructor seats can record a performance trace kept locally by default.
Studio shows a "AI가 지금 붐벼요" banner when the Service reports degraded upstream.
The first entry into a lesson shows the capability card (REQ-CGP-AGENT-03) once, with a 다음 action.

In the learner-page preview, the learner can add up to 10 numbered annotations, each an element pick (CR-09) or a dragged rectangle, with a short comment each, and send them together as one coach request.

After the coach finishes a turn that changed the learner's page, the preview shows a review bar for that turn: the number of changed files and units (from `diffGuard`), and **되돌리기** (revert the whole turn to the version before it) and **이대로 둘게요** (keep).
Closing the preview, or switching activity, while unsent annotations exist asks to keep or discard them.

In Chalk, an instructor can select a section of a `chalk-plan/1` plan (any element carrying a `data-chalk-*` marker) and attach a revision request to it. The generator revises only that section, and the result opens in the existing version compare (FB-01).

An instructor can leave a comment anchored to a place in a learner's approved artifact version (U1b). The learner sees it on that version in Studio and can reply or mark it handled. The coach is never assigned automatically.

For a picked element, the learner can adjust a small set of style properties (text color, background, font size, spacing, corner radius) with a live preview, then send the chosen values to the coach as a structured edit request. The tool does not write CSS itself.

When page context (`page_context`) or an element capture is attached to a turn, the learner sees exactly the text that will be sent, labeled with its source page origin, and can remove it before sending.

For minor cohorts (`browser_session.mode = "safe"`), every link the learner opens from chat or preview opens inside the integrated safe-session browser, never the system browser. A link outside the allowlist shows a blocked notice and does not navigate. For adult cohorts, opening a link in the system browser first shows a confirmation with the host.

When the learner's preview fails to load, the preview tab shows one cause line in learner language from `previewRecovery`'s classification (server not running, page missing (404), computer offline) and one action.
When the coach builds or changes the learner's page, the chat shows one result card with a thumbnail, page title, short version id, verified state per CR-81, and actions **열기** and **폴더에서 보기**.
Every published test version shows one persistent sharing-state label next to the page: who can open it, until when, and how many links are active.

The first time a learner publishes a test version, Studio shows a short responsibility notice. For minor cohorts with the institutional flag (SX-41), the instructor must confirm before the link opens.
For each test version, the learner sees counts of opened sessions and completed tasks for the last 7 days, compared with the previous 7 days. Each count opens its source sessions (CR-27).

When the learner asks for a page or deck "style" without naming one, the coach may offer up to 6 instructor-provided starter styles as a visual picker with preview images. The learner may pick one, upload their own reference image or file, or skip.
The learner can present the deck full-screen from the deck view with next and previous slide (keys and buttons), a position indicator, and exit. Speaker notes stay hidden from the audience.
A slide offers up to 3 suggestion chips (쉽게 줄이기, 그림으로 보이기, 핵심 강조). Each produces a CR-56 patch proposal for that slide only, which the student accepts or rejects.
While the coach is editing the learner's page, a **따라 보기** toggle (on by default) scrolls the preview to the most recently changed element after each live reload.
In image edit (REQ-STUDIO-IMAGE-EDIT), the learner can mark one or more regions on the image (rectangle or brush) and attach a comment to each. They are sent as region masks with the edit request.
When a coach turn has produced no new visible progress for 20 s, the progress line adds "평소보다 오래 걸리고 있어요" and a **멈추기** action. After 60 s it adds what is still running (tool name).
Each task shows a "AI가 한 일" summary: files read, created and changed, web pages opened, and searches, each expandable to the list.

When the coach asks approval to overwrite an existing workspace file, the approval modal shows a before and after summary (units changed and share changed, from `diffGuard`) before the learner approves.
Chalk shows a class-results view: one card per learner with the latest approved artifact version, thumbnail, approval time, and open. It has grid and list layouts and a filter for "승인 없음".
The learner can export the deck as a single PDF and open their page's folder from the result card.

An interactive block appears for a learner only when the confirmed lesson version attaches it to the current `SessionDesign` step (`steps[].materials[]`); the coach cannot insert one on its own in v1.
A block never sits in the work canvas and never shows capability names, scores, grades or "correct/incorrect" judgments.
Every block exposes a live text equivalent: a title, a controls help sentence, and a state description that updates on each change.
Block references in a confirmed lesson pin `type`, `version` and parameter values; the validator rejects unknown types, unknown versions and out-of-range values.
Stage-stepper blocks advance only on learner action and show one step's title + one sentence at a time.
Parameter and mode controls are bounded by the type schema and re-state the result in the caption after every change.
Animated blocks start paused; play is an explicit action and step-by-step is always available.
In a sampling block, the learner writes an expectation before the first batch; the result is shown beside the learner's own sentence, without a verdict.
Narrated diagrams attached by Chalk follow the 3-beat format with separable, localizable text layers.
A learner can reset a block to its preset and undo the last change.
A learner can report "자료가 틀린 것 같아요" on a block; the report reaches the lesson owner with block identity, and the learner can collapse a block they do not want.
Chalk offers a block picker filtered by the lesson's `audience_tier` and subject family, showing a thumbnail, title and one-line purpose.
When minor-cohort input is blocked for self-harm, the learner sees Korean help lines and the class instructor gets an immediate safety signal without conversation text.
Chalk first run asks the instructor once for grade band and subject and pre-fills the lesson audience.
Chalk's "completion checklist" helper produces observable acceptance items, never points or grade levels.
The Studio header shows one coach run state from a fixed set: 준비됨 / 생각 중 / 찾는 중 / 만드는 중 / 확인이 필요해요 / 멈춤 / 문제가 생겼어요.
Chalk help-request queue supports keyboard triage: next, previous, open, resolve-and-advance.

Optional start/stop earcons for dictation and voice

Each assistant answer can be read aloud on demand

A learner-level shortcut sheet lists only chat-panel shortcuts

Approvals may offer a "this conversation" scope; never "always" for minors

An instructor can freeze the Studio version for a cohort for a date range.

Native menus, native dialogs and settings labels a learner can reach are shown in Korean.

Before sending, a pass holder sees the remaining requests in the pass and when that number was confirmed.

The issuer page accepts a pasted or CSV roster and reports a result per row.
At first join, the learner acknowledges the class rules, and the time is recorded for the instructor.

Token file `tokens.css` is imported first; semantic names follow `--hp-{text|bg|border|ring}-{role}-{state}`

Mapping, for example: `--hp-text: var(--vscode-foreground, #F2F4E8)`, `--hp-ring: var(--vscode-focusBorder, #D5F279)`, `--hp-bg: var(--vscode-sideBar-background, #151D19)`, `--hp-code-bg: var(--vscode-textCodeBlock-background, …)`
Hover = text color at 8%, pressed 12–16% (light) or 12–20% (dark) over the surface; control boundary token ≥3:1
Status chip: 16px icon + 14px label, 4px radius, 8px inline padding, soft background
Learner scale: 14 / 16 / 18 / 22 / 28px; line-height 1.5 (labels), **1.65–1.75 (Hangul prose)**; tracking 0 for Hangul; weights 400/600 only
Text size: 16 / 18 / 20px body; controls scale proportionally; 44px targets unchanged
Spacing ladder 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32px; control heights 32 (non-learner dense), 44 (learner default), 48 (primary CTA)
Radii 4 / 8 / 12 / 16 / 24 / full; composer 16–24px; user bubble 16–20px; dialog 12px

`--hp-dur-press 140ms`, `--hp-dur-enter 180ms`, `--hp-dur-confirm 160ms`, `--hp-dur-move 240ms`; enter `cubic-bezier(.19,1,.22,1)`, exit `cubic-bezier(.4,0,1,1)`; no springs or bounces on learner surfaces
Reduced-motion state is on `<html data-reduced-motion=true|false>` set by the host; CSS gates with `:not([data-reduced-motion])` plus the media query
Forced colors: buttons `border:1px solid ButtonText`, bubbles `border:1px solid CanvasText`, focus `outline-color: Highlight`
Focus: `outline: 2px solid var(--hp-ring); outline-offset: 2px`; inset −2px inside scroll containers
Icon sizes 16 (inline), 20 (toolbar), 24 (empty states); 1.5–2px stroke; `currentColor`; status glyphs move from Unicode to icons with the same labels
Composer: radius 20px, min-height 48px, padding 12px, send button 44×44 inside; placeholder uses `--hp-text-muted` (≥4.5:1), not opacity
Prose max-width 40em; user bubble radius 18px, background = text at 6–8%, max-width 85%; assistant unboxed with an 18px identity mark
Chalk list rows ≥44px; actions are persistent icon+label buttons; scroll fade mask 16px top, 32px bottom
Menu: radius 12px, 4px gutter, items 44px (learner) / 32px (Chalk dense), 14px text, separator 1px border token
Dialog 320–480px, radius 12px, padding 20–24px, backdrop dim 40% dark / 30% light, enter 180ms, exit 120ms; ≤390px becomes a bottom sheet
Tooltip: 14px, radius 8px, padding 4×8, delay 500ms hover / immediate on focus; shortcut shown as text
Toast: bottom of the chat pane, content-width ≤ 360px, 14px, icon + text; success auto-hides at 4s; error persists
IME guard covers Enter, Escape, Tab, Arrow-up history and Cmd/Ctrl+Enter
Diff: `+`/`−` gutter glyph plus green/red tint at ≤15% alpha; removed text also struck through
